articles.title: Houge Park Facility Storage Cleanup
articles.summary: The Houge Park Facility Storage, used by various SJAA programs, underwent a much-needed cleanup and reorganization. Proposed and approved in 2019, the effort was carried out by several members in October 2020, leading to designated and locked storage for valuable items and improved overall organization.

articles.title: November Armchair Star Party
articles.summary: The SJAA Armchair Star Party returned in November after a three-month summer hiatus. This virtual event showcased five celestial objects: Mars, the Wizard nebula, the Elephant trunk nebula, the Owl/ET cluster, and the Andromeda galaxy. The event was supported by a team of hosts and interns, with plans to resume Armchair events next year.

articles.title: Lemonade from lemons in the heart of Auriga
articles.summary: The author embarked on an astrophotography trip to Pinnacles West during the October New Moon, initially hoping to image IC342 at high resolution. Despite meticulous equipment preparation, poor seeing conditions forced a change of plans. Adapting to the 'twinkly' stars, the author switched to a smaller telescope and successfully captured images of IC405 and IC410 in Auriga, turning a challenging night into a productive one.

articles.title: The Sky Shed
articles.summary: The author recounts his experience building a Sky Shed backyard observatory in 2004, detailing the challenges of site selection, sourcing materials from generic hardware stores instead of specialized lumberyards, and improvising construction techniques. Despite the amateur process and difficulties, the rolling-roof observatory, built over weekends, proved functional and durable for over four years, demonstrating that a personal observatory is an achievable project for enthusiasts.

articles.title: Earth and Moon Once Shared a Magnetic Shield, Protecting Their Atmospheres
articles.summary: A NASA-led study suggests that 4 to 3.5 billion years ago, Earth and the Moon shared connected magnetic fields, creating a combined shield against the Sun's harsh radiation and solar wind. This lunar protection was critical for Earth to retain its early atmosphere, eventually enabling the development of life. The research also indicates atmospheric exchange between the two bodies and highlights the importance of future Artemis missions to collect samples from the lunar South Pole to further test these findings.

articles.title: Solar Cycle 25 Is Here. NASA, NOAA Scientists Explain What That Means
articles.summary: NASA and NOAA scientists have officially announced the start of Solar Cycle 25, with the solar minimum occurring in December 2019. This new cycle signifies an upcoming increase in solar activity, predicted to reach its maximum in July 2025, which will bring heightened space weather. Experts emphasize the importance of understanding and preparing for these changes, as increased solar activity can impact technology on Earth, as well as astronauts and spacecraft during missions like Artemis.

articles.title: Kid Spot
articles.summary: This "Kid Spot" article features a collection of astronomy and physics-themed jokes, designed to entertain and offer a lighthearted take on scientific concepts. It also includes brief "Did You Know?" sections, providing fascinating facts about significant astronomical phenomena. These facts cover the large-scale gamma-ray structures known as Fermi Bubbles near the Galactic center and the intensely magnetic neutron stars called Magnetars.

articles.title: From the Board of Directors
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is adapting its operations due to the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to event cancellations, a shift to online formats for some activities like the Armchair Star Party, and the rescheduling of the Fall Swap Meet. The article also announces upcoming online elections for both board members and officer positions in February and March 2021, and provides excerpts from recent board meetings detailing calendar progress, volunteer projects, and the status of the loaner program.

articles.title: SJAA Library
articles.summary: The article details a variety of programs and resources offered by the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) for its members and the wider community. These include a library, equipment loaner program, and services like telescope 'Fix It' sessions. SJAA also hosts numerous educational initiatives and events such as solar observing, 'Quick STARt' sessions for beginners, 'Intro to the Night Sky' events, astro imaging groups and workshops, and school star parties, catering to all ages and skill levels in amateur astronomy.
